In [[mathematics]], specifically in [[category theory]], a [[functor]] 

:<math>F:C\to D</math> 

is '''essentially surjective''' if each object <math>d</math> of <math>D</math> is isomorphic to an object of the form <math>Fc</math> for some object <math>c</math> of <math>C</math>.

Any functor that is part of an [[equivalence of categories]] is essentially surjective. As a partial converse, any [[full and faithful functor]] that is essentially surjective is part of an equivalence of categories.<ref>Mac Lane (1998), Theorem IV.4.1</ref>
